snip.t: MRI is the study of choice to evaluate degree of spinal cord compression and identify myelomalacia
Emergencies: SVC obstruction, spinal cord compression, hypercalcaemia, massive haemoptysis, tracheal obstruction.
Neurological: Neck stiffness, altered mental status, focal neurological deficits (meningeal TB, spinal cord compression).
Presence of complications: Massive haemoptysis, respiratory failure, spinal cord compression, neurological deficits, cardiac tamponade.
Pathologic fractures / spinal cord compression: Focal bone pain, neurologic deficit — Orthopaedic fixation or radiotherapy, continue systemic therapy, immobilise
